dailyProtocol.strategy: Hydrate with 500ml water + electrolytes. Swim is kept 100% fasted.
The weekday's routine from the swim programme: 100 lengths of a 25m pool, 2-stroke alternating breathing, floor-free open turns. Doubles as the full thermal and joint warm-up for the gym.
200-250ml Leche Desnatada Omega-3 + 1 tbsp Miel Pura + a pinch of salt. Drink it while changing - it restores blood glucose without sitting heavy in the stomach.
3 to 4 exercises only. One light prep set, then straight into the first lift. Finish with the mandatory 60-second dead hang.
Full recovery meal: 35g-40g protein + complex carbs (e.g., 4 eggs + oatmeal or a whey smoothie). This is the real refuel, once the training is done.
Remote programming work. Afternoons reserved for tennis, basketball, or rest.

fuel.title: Locker-Room Transition Fuel
fuel.recipe: 200-250ml (0.20-0.25 L) Leche Desnatada Omega-3 + 1 tbsp Miel Pura + a pinch of salt.
fuel.why: Restores blood glucose and halts muscle breakdown immediately following 90 minutes of fasted swimming. Small enough to drink in the five minutes it takes to change, so there is no stomach sloshing or heaviness under a loaded bar minutes later.

warmUp.title: Warm-Up Protocol - The 2,500m Swim Is the Warm-Up
warmUp.execution: No separate gym warm-up. 90 minutes of swimming has already raised core temperature and lubricated the shoulder joints, and the 25-minute window has no room to spare. Go directly to the first lift after 1 light prep set at roughly half the working weight.

coolDown.title: Cool-Down & Spinal Decompression - Passive Bar Dead Hangs
coolDown.why: Heavy pressing and rowing compress the spine and tighten the upper back and shoulders. A dead hang reverses that compression, relaxes tight muscles, and resets posture.

prescription.note: Keep it passive - relax and let gravity pull the hips down. This is the one part of the session that is never skipped for time.

rules.title: The 3-Second Eccentric Rule (Controlled Barbell Lowering)
rules.body: At age 56, lowering heavy barbell weight uncontrollably increases shoulder and elbow tendon wear without extra muscle gain. Lower every bench press and curl over 3 slow seconds to maximize mechanical muscle tension while keeping joints completely safe.

rules.title: Barbell Pressing Path & Scapular Retraction
rules.body: Never press with flared elbows (90 degrees). On both the Flat and Incline Barbell Bench Press, tuck elbows to a 45-60 degree angle to the torso and keep shoulder blades pinched tightly together into the bench. This isolates the pecs and protects the rotator cuffs from swimmer's impingement.

rules.title: Keep 1 to 2 Reps in Reserve (RPE 8 Training Threshold)
rules.body: Do not train to absolute muscle failure on barbell presses. End the set when 1 or 2 more clean reps are still possible. This preserves central nervous system recovery for the 7:00 AM daily swims - and inside a 25-minute window, a set taken to failure costs more rest time than the extra rep is worth.

rules.title: Posterior Shoulder Counter-Balance
rules.body: Freestyle swimming and barbell chest pressing both tighten internal rotators (pectoralis major & lats). Never skip Rear Delt Flyes or Seated Rows - they pull the shoulder heads back into optimal joint alignment.

legTraining.title: Leg Training Is Deliberately Omitted
legTraining.body: No leg exercises are performed in the gym. Lower-body volume is already fully covered by daily swim kicks, tennis and basketball. Adding squats or leg presses to a 25-minute post-swim window would compete directly with recovery for the next morning's 2,500m swim, which is the foundation the whole program is built on.

workouts.name: Day 1: Flat Chest Mass & Push Focus
workouts.focus: Flat barbell chest, machine press volume, outer tricep, rear delts

exercises.name: Flat Barbell Bench Press
exercises.target: Overall Chest / Sternal Pecs, Delts & Triceps
cues: Lock in scapular retraction (pinch shoulder blades down & back into bench).
Lower bar to mid-lower sternum; press upward in slight arc toward eye level.
Keep 45 degree elbow tuck to protect swimmer's rotator cuff joints.

exercises.name: Flat Machine Chest Press
cues: Provides safe hyper-isolation volume following heavy barbell benching.
Focus on squeezing inner chest together without locking elbows hard.

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Pressdown Machine
cues: Keep torso locked against the pad and push down through the heels of your hands.
Backup (Plan B): If occupied, immediately swap to the Cable Rope Tricep Pushdown to avoid queuing.
Never do this before the pressing work - fresh triceps are what hold up the bench press.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck (Rear Delt Fly)
cues: Sit facing pad. Drive handles backward using rear shoulders.
Protects shoulders against swimmer's forward posture imbalance.

workouts.name: Day 2: Upper Back & Biceps Peak
workouts.focus: Upper back thickness, biceps peak, brachialis

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Machine Row (or Seated Cable Row)
exercises.benefit: Zero lower back strain; 100% upper back
cues: Drive elbows outward wide to balance heavy swim pulling forces.
Keep chest firmly pressed against pad throughout entire set.

exercises.name: Standing Supinating Dumbbell Curls
cues: Keep elbows stationary at your sides; turn palm outward at peak contraction.
Avoid body swing to keep tension strictly on biceps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curls
cues: Pushes biceps upward for thicker overall arm appearance.
Avoid swinging; lower under complete control (2-3 seconds).

exercises.name: Machine Preacher Curl OR Machine Shrug
cues: Execute only one of these machines to keep the session at a strict 4 exercises and stay within the 25-minute window.
If Preacher Curl: Lock armpits securely into the pad to eliminate all momentum and isolate the biceps.
If Machine Shrug: Elevate shoulders straight up toward the ears with zero shoulder rotation to safely build upper back thickness.

workouts.name: Day 3: Upper Chest, Triceps & Posterior Shoulder
workouts.focus: Incline barbell chest, inner chest, tricep long head, posterior delts

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.target: Upper Chest / Clavicular Pecs & Front Delts
cues: Set bench angle strictly to 30 degrees (minimizes front shoulder strain).
Tuck elbows at 45 to 60 degrees to body; do not flare out to 90 degrees.
Touch bar to upper collarbone/sternum area without bouncing off chest.

exercises.name: Pec Deck Machine Fly
cues: Sit facing away from the machine; adjust seat height so handles align directly with mid-chest.
Maintain a slight, rigid flex in elbows; drive handles together in front of sternum, squeezing hard for 1 second at peak contraction.

exercises.name: Seated DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.benefit: Maximum long-head stretch with zero cable setup
cues: Sit on a backed bench; cup one dumbbell overhead with both hands, elbows pointing forward.
Lower behind head until the long head is fully stretched (3 seconds), then press up cleanly.
Keep upper arms fixed next to ears and ribs down; do not let elbows flare wide.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck (Machine Rear Delt Fly)
exercises.benefit: Posterior delt shield against swim strain
cues: Sit facing the chest pad; keep chest against the pad and shoulder blades stable.
Drive handles backward wide using the rear shoulders to shield rotator cuffs against swim strain.

swappingMatrix.anchorNote: B1 (Flat Barbell Bench Press, Day 1) and A1 (Incline Barbell Bench Press, Day 3) are non-negotiable anchor lifts to be done first. Because they use heavy loads in the 6-8 rep range, doing them late in a 25-minute session after the chest and triceps are fatigued increases injury risk and degrades strength gains.

items.note: Always secure the bench rack first, while the central nervous system is still fresh from the swim.
Day 2's only compound pull, so it opens the session. If the chest-supported machine is occupied, switch to the seated cable row - same 8-10 prescription, no waiting.
Machine chest volume in the 10-12 range. If the machine is busy, move to that day's tricep or rear delt work and come back - the strength progression lives on the barbell, not here.

tiers.label: Fully Swappable (Do Anywhere Near the End)

items.note: For Day 1 (A5), use the Triceps Pressdown Machine as Plan A, or immediately swap to the rope if occupied. For Day 3 (B5), it needs only a dumbbell and a backed bench, so it never waits on equipment. Golden rule: never do tricep isolation before that day's pressing (B1/A3 on Day 1, A1 on Day 3).
Pure arm/back isolation. These can be done in any sequence during the second half of Day 2.
Day 1 and Day 3 both finish on the reverse pec deck. Low-risk, high-rep isolation that fits almost any open slot; if the machine is taken, substitute a bench-supported dumbbell rear delt fly.

swappingMatrix.goldenRule: In a 25-minute window there is no time to queue for a machine. If the rack is not open for B1/A1, start with that day's machine work or rear delts and come back to the bar - just hold off on tricep isolation until the pressing is done.

schedule.objective: Active chest opening & shoulder alignment; prevents rotator impingement.
Aerobic threshold conditioning & speed control via 10x100m intervals.
Mental engagement & progressive block pacing (700m down to 300m).
Mid-week active joint recovery & external rotation balancing.
Distance-per-stroke maintenance under controlled aerobic fatigue.
Sustained endurance & stroke count tracking across 1,500m Free block.
Volume endurance with shrinking block structure.

routines.name: The Interleaved Circuit
routines.target: Shoulder rotator balance & active posture reset

blocks.title: Freestyle
blocks.detail: Steady cruise pace. 2-stroke breathing, alternating side per length.

blocks.title: Breaststroke
blocks.detail: Smooth glide pace; active upper-body rest.

blocks.title: Backstroke
blocks.detail: Active chest opener to stretch pectorals and reset shoulders.
blocks.rest: 30 seconds at wall before starting next round.

blocks.title: Block 2 - Main Pace Interval
points: Rest: exactly 15 seconds at wall after each 100m.
Pacing: sets 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 = Cruise pace. Sets 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 = Brisk pace (effort 7-8/10).

blocks.title: Block 1 - Long Freestyle Block
blocks.detail: Continuous swim at steady cruise pace. Count strokes on length 10, length 30 and length 50 to verify stroke length consistency.

blocks.title: Block 2 - Breaststroke Block
blocks.detail: Continuous swim focusing on maximum kick propulsion and glide distance per stroke.

blocks.title: Block 3 - Backstroke Cool-Down
blocks.detail: Continuous relaxed backstroke to open chest and decompress shoulders.

express.title: Emergency Backup Routine: Modular Express Set
express.intro: For days when work or life limits pool time. A flexible 400m main block scales to the time available.

mainBlock.title: Modular Main Block
mainBlock.detail: 4 x 100m (50m Freestyle Brisk Pace + 50m Breast or Back Recovery Pace). Take 15 seconds rest at wall after each 100m.

express.note: You are free to swap Breaststroke and Backstroke during recovery lengths whenever your shoulders or knees need a change.

points.label: 2-Stroke Alternating Pattern
points.text: Breathe every 2 strokes, alternating your breathing side every 25m length (e.g., breathe right going down, breathe left coming back).

points.label: Neuromuscular & Joint Balance
points.text: Alternating sides per length prevents asymmetrical neck/shoulder strain while maintaining distance-per-stroke symmetry.

points.label: Why Not 3-Stroke
points.text: Breathing every 2 strokes maintains steady, high oxygen saturation. Bilateral 3-stroke breathing reduces breathing frequency by 33%, causing air starvation during longer blocks. Stick strictly to 2-stroke alternating.

openTurn.title: Open Turn Technique (Floor-Free Pivot)
openTurn.intro: Never step or stand on the pool floor during turns. Stepping causes sudden joint impact on ankles and knees, breaks forward momentum, and places torsional stress on the lower back.

steps.action: Touch wall with one hand (Free/Back) or both hands (Breast) at surface level without grabbing edge.
Allow momentum to bring hips toward wall. Tuck knees tightly to chest underwater (no floor contact).
Rotate body sideways and plant both feet flat against wall, 30-50cm below surface.
Push off horizontally in full streamline position (arms locked overhead, hands stacked) before rotating into stroke.

points.label: Immediate Resumption
points.text: If you miss one or several days, resume immediately on the workout scheduled for the day you return. Never attempt to make up missed volume or stack workouts.

points.label: Extended Absences (>5 Days)
points.text: Keep intensity at 70% effort for the first two sessions upon return to allow shoulder internal/external rotators to re-acclimate safely.

summaryStrategy: The 7:00 AM swim is the untouchable physical and mental foundation: 2,500m every morning on a fixed weekday rotation of four routines, and it also serves as the gym warm-up. Five minutes of locker-room fuel bridges it to a 20-25 minute gym micro-session three mornings a week, so all eleven exercises still get their full volume in sessions short enough to sustain on top of daily swimming. Heavy compound barbell pressing drives upper body mass, strict upper back pulling and posterior shoulder isolation keep the joints aligned against swimmer's forward posture, and every session closes with a 60-second passive dead hang. Legs are trained by the pool and the tennis and basketball courts, never in the gym.
